## RCA — root cause CONFIRMED at runtime (Phase 1 exit)

### Proven mechanism

Decorate-then-fit ordering. The marker is appended as the LAST characters of the
outbound body, and every comment fitter truncates from the RIGHT, so the marker is
always the first thing cut.

1. `outbound_comments.py:205` — `_decorate_outbound_comment` returns
   `f"{body}\n\n{RECONCILER_MARKER}"`; the marker is the tail of the string.
2. `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:516` — the ONE live Cloud comment send path:
   `body_arg = json.dumps(codec.to_wire(codec.fit_outbound(body)))`. `fit_outbound`
   receives the ALREADY-DECORATED body and truncates it.
3. `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` binary-searches the largest `text[:mid] + _ADF_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX`
   whose serialized ADF fits `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32000` — a right-truncation, so
   the trailing marker paragraph is discarded.

### Runtime evidence (not read from source — observed executing)

Driving a 40,000-char body through each real fitter (`.venv`, worktree `fix-illadopsis-marker`):

```
decorated len: 40032   ends with marker: True
A) current Cloud ADF send path -> fitted len 31887 | marker in fitted: False
                                | marker in RENDERED ADF: False
                                | tail: 'xxxx … [truncated by reconciler]'
B) rich=True ADF send path      -> marker in fitted: False
C) comment_limits.truncate_comment_body -> len 32767 | marker present: False
                                | tail: 'xxxx … [truncated by reconciler]'
D) DC WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound        -> len 32767 | marker present: False
```

All four fitters drop it. A short body keeps it, so the loss is length-triggered.

### The loop-breaker is provably inert (dynamic claim, observed)

Feeding the landed wire back through the inbound side
(`adf.adf_to_text` -> the `RECONCILER_MARKER in body_text` test at
`inbound_collection_diffs.py:148`):

```
short        -> inbound loop-breaker sees marker: True
over-length  -> inbound loop-breaker sees marker: False
```

So an over-length outbound echo is NOT recognised as ours on the next inbound pass —
exactly the loop the marker exists to break, disabled for precisely the comments most
likely to loop.

### The production signature matches experiment C exactly

The 836 marker-less duplicates (REB-1567 x418, REB-1931 x278, REB-2605 x140) are
**exactly 32767 chars ending in `" … [truncated by reconciler]"`** — byte-identical to
experiment C's `truncate_comment_body` output, i.e. the plaintext `_sanitize_comment`
send path that preceded the ADF-encode change (`27b868ba55`, 2026-08-13,
emersed-specific-mutt). That both dates the damage and confirms the mechanism is not
specific to today's fitter: it survived a send-path rewrite because the ORDERING, not
the fitter, is the defect.

### Defect legitimacy: `defect` (cited)

The behaviour violates an explicit, checked-in design invariant:

- `outbound_comments.py:72-78` — "marker token embedded in **every** outbound comment
  body ... Without the marker every outbound comment would re-appear inbound as a 'new
  Jira comment' and the bridge would loop."
- `_decorate_outbound_comment` docstring (`:198-204`) — "The marker survives ADF
  round-trip."
- Existing test `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_comments_diff.py:197`
  asserts `decorated.endswith(RECONCILER_MARKER)` and `:210` asserts the marker is in
  the emitted body — the contract is pinned, just never exercised over-length.

### Defect origin: UNATTRIBUTABLE (close class `preexisting`)

Date test applied. Both implicated sites blame (`git blame -w -C -M`) to
**`b534f47a7f` (2026-06-08) "Extract DSO ticket system + Jira reconciler into standalone
rebar"** — the repo's import commit (its parent `337ff71fdc` contains only `README.md`).
It carries no `rebar-ticket:` trailer.

The marker (`RECONCILER_MARKER`, DSO "Gap 1"/bug 85a1) and the comment truncation
(DSO bug 6afc-20ee-84e5-4dd5) arrived together in that single import, so there is no
later change that broke previously-working behaviour and no obligation-creating commit
inside this repo's history.

Searches that came up empty:
- `rebar show 6afc-20ee-84e5-4dd5` -> `ticket_not_found`; likewise `85a1`. `rebar search`
  returns only OTHER tickets that cite those DSO-era ids in prose, not the tickets.
- `git log -S'def truncate_comment_body'`, `-S'def _decorate_outbound_comment'`,
  `-S'RECONCILER_MARKER = "<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->"'` -> all bottom out at `b534f47a7f`.
- `git log --follow -- adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` -> same.

Divergence from the whole-file blame default: none to report — blame and the date test
agree, and both land on an untrailered pre-history import.

Explicitly NOT attributed to `27b868ba55` / emersed-specific-mutt: the 32767-char
production evidence predates it and proves the defect already existed.
